text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: llm4rec-far-trans/Vladislav/session3/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md
+# FAR-Trans Homework 3 experiment results
+
+## Run status and reproducibility
+
+The 100-user HW2 regression and the 2,000-user HW3 paired comparison completed. All four classical baselines reproduced the saved HW2 aggregate metrics at full precision, and one-hot reproduced Vladislav’s saved row at full precision. The four classical methods also matched an independent run of the unchanged starter on all 2,000 users, including every recommended ISIN and rank. The original-text TF-IDF control completed. The instructor’s LLM-Rec Encoder run is in progress.
+
+Both are development cohorts. The starter selects warm users with as-of profiles and eligible pre-cutoff Buy history in ascending order of `SHA256("42:" + customerID)`, with customer ID breaking hash ties. The 100 users are the exact prefix of the 2,000. The cutoff is June 1, 2021. The evaluation window starts June 1 and ends July 1, exclusive. All 767 assets have pre-cutoff metadata and a positive pre-cutoff close price. Repeat recommendations and repeat future purchases are eligible. The starter excluded 38,019 reconstructed initial-position rows and found zero exact duplicate rows. All methods evaluate the same eligible Buy truth within each cohort. Empty truth contributes zero to the primary binary nDCG@10 mean. Only historical data enters scoring.
+
+| Cohort | Starter protocol SHA-256 |
+|---|---|
+| HW2 regression | `50efd4aeb415ba6f0c66dd0793a7c2033cdc32a42b86b58eebbca3e81eaf3417` |
+| HW3 development | `3340b8ae5c87987afba9adaa93902159d7c7106734ed1ac9dd78e32995a4470c` |
+
+The official University of Glasgow archive passed `unzip -tq`. The archive SHA-256 is `d0d6cfe027732bab45fdcf9af80eff4fefddc789aedae9bdce0d3d6cfd05cfb6`. The four source CSV hashes are recorded in each starter protocol. [Official FAR-Trans archive](https://researchdata.gla.ac.uk/1658/1/FAR-Trans.zip) · [100-user protocol](outputs/controls/regression100/protocol.json) · [2,000-user protocol](outputs/starter2000/protocol.json)
+
+**Code and machine.** The local repository base is `3a8ca8d52017792e640ac5a642d2119ec6be9ae7`, with the Homework 3 runners as local files. Ivan’s Session 3 README was read at team revision `57be29e0a24787fc7306b16738068c70b13916df` in an ignored checkout. Its MPS loading pattern informed the instructor adapter. The paired scorer and embedding inference reuse Vladislav’s and Ivan’s Session 2 implementations. Runs used a MacBook Pro `Mac16,7`, Apple M4 Pro with 14 CPU cores and 24 GB unified memory, macOS 27.2 build `26B123`, Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.11.0, Transformers 4.57.6, NumPy 2.5.5, tokenizers 0.22.2, Hugging Face Hub 0.36.2 and safetensors 0.8.0. The existing HW2 environment had the required packages. MPS was available outside the command sandbox. [Experiment runner](run_experiments.py) · [Reference runner](run_reference.py) · [Source hashes](outputs/source_sha256.txt) · [Dependency inventory](outputs/dependencies.txt)
+
+**Paired comparison.** Both arms use the latest pre-cutoff `assetCategory`, `assetSubCategory`, `sector` and `industry`. Blank, `Not_Available` and `nan` values map to `[MISSING]` after trimming and case-folding for the missing-value check. Each distinct past eligible Buy ISIN contributes one unit vector, including separate votes from different ISINs with identical tuples. The shared scorer averages history vectors and ranks all eligible assets by FP64 cosine to that centroid. Equal scores use descending distinct-buyer popularity, then ascending ISIN. The one-hot vocabulary is field-specific. The Qwen input is four labeled lines with JSON-quoted values.
+
+**Embedding inference.** `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` at `97b0c614be4d77ee51c0cef4e5f07c00f9eb65b3` ran offline on MPS in FP16 with SDPA, four Torch threads, seed 42, eight texts per batch, left padding, an 8,192-token bound, last-nonpadding-token pooling and FP32 unit normalization. The embedding call uses the plain four-line description and disables the model’s KV cache. The real forward-pass check returned two finite 1,024-dimensional unit vectors. The measured run encoded all 143 unique tuples across 767 assets in 18 batches and reused that matrix for both cohorts. The disk cache had 143 misses and zero hits for this initial run. The staging recovery resumed 840 MiB from the incomplete HW2 weight download and verified the completed weight against SHA-256 `0437e45c94563b09e13cb7a64478fc406947a93cb34a7e05870fc8dcd48e23fd`. [Embedding forward pass](outputs/embedding_smoke/forward_pass.json) · [Embedding cache and batch timings](outputs/main/run.json)
+
+**Instructor reference comparison.** `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` at `70d244cc86ccca08cf5af4e1e306ecf908b1ad5e` uses the shared `p_para` prompt on asset name, category, subcategory, sector, industry and market. The shared method forms separate original-text and paraphrase TF-IDF views, normalizes and concatenates them, and uses count-weighted pre-cutoff Buy profiles with ascending-ISIN score ties. The control uses the original-text view alone. Both score the full eligible universe. The reference uses greedy decoding, thinking disabled, an 8,192-token context bound, a 160-token generation cap, and the shared 1–40-word validation and original-text fallback. [Shared reference instructions](../../shared/far-trans-llm/README.md) · [Shared prompt and scorer](../../shared/far-trans-llm/encoder.py)
+
+### Commands
+
+Run from the repository root. The result directories in these commands were empty at execution time. Use fresh result directories to rerun completed stages. The saved embedding cache can be reused.
+
+```bash
+curl -fL --retry 3 --connect-timeout 20 --continue-at - \
+  --output data/FAR-Trans.zip https://researchdata.gla.ac.uk/1658/1/FAR-Trans.zip
+unzip -tq data/FAR-Trans.zip
+unzip -nq data/FAR-Trans.zip -d data
+
+Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -B -m unittest discover -s Vladislav/session2 -v
+Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -B -m unittest discover -s shared/far-trans -v
+Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -B -m unittest discover -s shared/far-trans-llm -p 'test_*.py' -v
+Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -Bu Vladislav/session3/run_experiments.py controls \
+  --output-dir Vladislav/session3/outputs/controls
+Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -Bu Vladislav/session3/run_experiments.py main --one-hot-only \
+  --output-dir Vladislav/session3/outputs/one_hot_only
+Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -Bu shared/far-trans/starter.py run --data-dir data/FAR-Trans \
+  --output-dir Vladislav/session3/outputs/starter2000 --max-users 2000
+
+env HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT=60 HF_HOME=Vladislav/session3/outputs/hf_http \
+  Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -Bu - <<'PY'
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
+pins = [
+    ('Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B', '97b0c614be4d77ee51c0cef4e5f07c00f9eb65b3'),
+    ('Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B', '70d244cc86ccca08cf5af4e1e306ecf908b1ad5e'),
+]
+def stage(pin):
+    model, revision = pin
+    return snapshot_download(model, revision=revision,
+                             allow_patterns=['*.safetensors', '*.json', '*.txt', '*.jinja'])
+with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool:
+    for snapshot in pool.map(stage, pins):
+        print(snapshot)
+PY
+
+env HF_HOME=Vladislav/session3/outputs/hf_http HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
+  Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -Bu Vladislav/session3/run_experiments.py embedding-smoke \
+  --output-dir Vladislav/session3/outputs/embedding_smoke
+env HF_HOME=Vladislav/session3/outputs/hf_http HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
+  Vladislav/session2/.venv/bin/python -Bu Vladislav/session3/run_experiments.py main \
+  --output-dir Vladislav/session3/outputs/main
+```
+
+### Saved evidence
+

+
+The native Codex JSONL and its local snapshot contain the experiment session. Raw data, weights, generation caches, prompts and customer-level evidence remain in ignored local directories. [Local session snapshot](outputs/native_session_snapshot.jsonl)
+
+## Results
+
+### HW2 regression, original 100 warm users
+
+| Method | Evaluated users | Nonempty truth | Mean nDCG@10, all | Mean nDCG@10, nonempty |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

+
+### HW3 development, first 2,000 warm users
+
+| Method | Evaluated users | Nonempty truth | Mean nDCG@10, all | Mean nDCG@10, nonempty |

+| Popularity | 2,000 | 234 | 0.0299 | 0.2555 |

+| Instructor LLM-Rec Encoder, reference | In progress | — | — | — |
+
+### Timing and output coverage
+
+Wall times are measured seconds from the completed stages. Preparation and ranking rows exclude staging downloads, metric aggregation, output serialization and case analysis. The two shared preparation scopes have separate process startups. [Classical and original-text timings](outputs/controls/run.json) · [Paired timings](outputs/main/run.json)
+
+| Stage | Scope | Seconds |
+|---|---|---:|
+| Preparation | Controls data load, ordered user selection, hashes and popularity counts | 1.4013 |
+| Preparation | Starter feature construction and recency event scan | 0.9655 |
+| Preparation | Independent 100-user starter verification including its own ranking and outputs | 2.5925 |
+| Preparation | Original text serialization and TF-IDF, full universe | 0.0060 |
+| Preparation | Paired-run data load, ordered user selection, hashes and popularity counts | 1.3555 |
+| Preparation | Paired-run four-field tuple and history mapping | 0.0018 |
+| Preparation | One-hot representation, shared by both cohorts | 0.0002 |
+| Preparation and inference | Qwen3 representation wall time, including imports, checkpoint load, encoding and cache I/O, once for both cohorts | 6.0630 |
+| Inference within the Qwen3 wall time | Checkpoint load 0.4906 s. Encoding wall time 2.4082 s, including 2.3526 s of synchronized MPS batch compute | 2.4082 |
+| Recommendation generation | Popularity and classical CBF together, including starter context construction, 2,000 users | 1.5909 |
+| Recommendation generation | Both classical recency baselines together, 2,000 users | 0.3096 |
+| Recommendation generation | Original-text TF-IDF control, 2,000 users | 1.3502 |
+| Recommendation generation | One-hot, 100 users / 2,000 users | 0.0155 / 0.3020 |
+| Recommendation generation | Qwen3, 100 users / 2,000 users | 0.0189 / 0.3591 |
+
+Every completed classical, paired and original-text control ranking had ten eligible distinct ISINs. These methods had zero invalid rankings. The paired arms used zero model fallbacks. Classical CBF and original-text TF-IDF each used zero zero-score popularity fallbacks on the development cohort. The starter’s normal recency fill used popularity for 1,835 Latest buy lists and 1,794 Latest buy or sell lists that had fewer than ten distinct eligible historical assets under their respective event rules. The four metadata fields were present for 767, 514, 401 and 356 assets, respectively.
+
+## Research question · One to three distinct past buys
+
+Of the 2,000 development users, 1,378 had one to three distinct eligible past buys. The history-size counts were 847 with one, 341 with two and 190 with three. There were 55 users with nonempty truth and 1,323 with empty truth. Each Qwen win or loss compares both methods on the same user’s full-precision nDCG@10. [Paired subgroup output](outputs/main/development2000/short_history.json)
+
+| Subgroup | Users | One-hot mean | Qwen3 mean | Mean paired Qwen3 minus one-hot | Qwen wins | Qwen losses | Ties |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| All short-history users | 1,378 | 0.0193 | 0.0190 | −0.0003 | 11 | 9 | 1,358 |
+| Short-history users with nonempty truth | 55 | 0.4841 | 0.4769 | −0.0073 | 11 | 9 | 35 |
+
+## Failure analysis
+
+Ranks below are full-universe ranks. Each case includes the pre-cutoff history’s fields, eligible labels, exact scores and popularity counts in the saved evidence. [Case details](outputs/main/development2000/cases.json)
+
+- **Qwen helps, Case 01.** The user previously bought `GRS426003000`, a large-cap energy stock, which both methods rank first and which appears again in the label window. Qwen moves the other future Buy, `GRS393503008`, from rank 10 to 7, increasing nDCG@10 from `0.7904` to `0.8175`. Its stock category and large-cap subcategory match the past purchase. Its sector and industry differ. One-hot gives it `0.500000` and ranks it by popularity within that score group. Qwen gives it `0.775243`, above Qwen’s rank-10 score of `0.761786`. The evidence shows a change in relative ordering. A semantic association between the businesses is a possible explanation.
+- **Qwen hurts, Case 02.** The user’s only past Buy was `GRS015003007`, a large-cap regional bank. The sole future Buy, `GRS003003035`, has missing sector and industry. One-hot ranks it ninth on cosine `0.500000` with 3,662 past buyers among the tied large-cap stocks. Qwen places it 15th on `0.723494`, below rank-10 `US9497461015`, a diversified bank with cosine `0.768129`. nDCG@10 drops from `0.3010` to `0.0000`. The lower score directly explains the exclusion. The missing fields may have affected its position.
+- **Qwen leaves relevant buys outside the Top 10, Case 03.** The relevant `GRS472003011`, `GRS475003018` and `GRS498003003` all share `Stock / [MISSING] / Technology / Software - Application`. They and two other assets in the same score group have identical Qwen cosine `0.843066230800981`. Among these three relevant assets, the historical buyer counts are 113, 82 and 80. The popularity tie-break puts them at Qwen ranks 10, 13 and 14. One-hot put them at ranks 5, 8 and 9. The tuple collision is observed. It makes their representation identical, so the shared tie-break determines which relevant assets survive the boundary.
+
+## Hand-check case · Case 01
+
+Case 01 has one distinct eligible past Buy, `GRS426003000`. The eligible future Buy IDs are `GRS393503008` and `GRS426003000`. The full score files include each asset’s rank, cosine, historical buyer count and four fields. [One-hot scores](outputs/main/development2000/case-01-one_hot-scores.json) · [Qwen3 scores](outputs/main/development2000/case-01-qwen3-scores.json) · [Local case-to-customer lookup](outputs/main/development2000/case_customer_ids.json)
+
+| Rank | Four-field one-hot | Qwen3 four-field encoder |
+|---:|---|---|
+| 1 | **GRS426003000** | **GRS426003000** |
+| 2 | GRS298343005 | GRS298343005 |
+| 3 | GRS473003002 | GRS473003002 |
+| 4 | GRS477003008 | GRS477003008 |
+| 5 | GRS003003035 | GRS191213008 |
+| 6 | GRS015003007 | GRS145003000 |
+| 7 | GRS014003032 | **GRS393503008** |
+| 8 | GRS323003012 | GRS518003009 |
+| 9 | GRS434003000 | GRS260333000 |
+| 10 | **GRS393503008** | GRS470003013 |
+
+For a hand calculation, a relevant item at rank `r` contributes `1/log2(r + 1)`. Divide the sum of the two hit gains by the ideal gain for hits at ranks 1 and 2. The saved evaluation values are `0.7903864795495061` for one-hot and `0.8175295903539445` for Qwen3.

+"""Verify saved rankings, labels, metrics, protocols and manual case evidence."""
+from collections import defaultdict

+
+
+def read(path):
+    return json.loads(path.read_text())
+
+
+def rankings(path):
+    result = defaultdict(dict)
+    with path.open(newline='') as stream:
+        for row in csv.DictReader(stream):
+            method = result[row['method']]
+            order = method.setdefault(row['user_id'], [])
+            assert int(row['rank']) == len(order) + 1
+            order.append(row['ISIN'])
+    return result
+
+
+def verify_method_files(path, protocol, data):
+    assert read(path / 'protocol.json') == protocol
+    users = protocol['users']
+    eligible = set(protocol['eligible_assets'])
+    saved = read(path / 'per_user.json')
+    measured = read(path / 'metrics.json')
+    prediction = rankings(path / 'predictions.csv')
+    assert list(measured) == list(prediction)
+    assert len(saved) == len(users) * len(measured)
+    rows = {(row['method'], row['user_id']): row for row in saved}
+    for method, user_ranks in prediction.items():
+        assert list(user_ranks) == users
+        for uid, order in user_ranks.items():
+            assert len(order) == len(set(order)) == 10 and set(order) <= eligible
+            truth = data.truth.get(uid, set()) & eligible
+            row = rows[method, uid]
+            assert row['relevant_count'] == len(truth)
+            assert row['ndcg_at_10'] == starter.ndcg10(order, truth)
+        assert measured[method] == starter.aggregate([rows[method, uid] for uid in users])
+    return prediction, rows
+
+
+def main():
+    data = Evaluation.load(hw2.ROOT / 'data/FAR-Trans')
+    summary = {}
+    for name, length in COHORTS.items():
+        controls = OUT / 'controls' / name
+        main = OUT / 'main' / name
+        protocol = read(controls / 'protocol.json')
+        users = data.users[:length]
+        assert protocol['users'] == users and data.data_hashes == protocol['source_sha256']
+        payload = {k: v for k, v in protocol.items() if k != 'protocol_hash'}
+        assert hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest() == protocol['protocol_hash']
+        control_preds, _ = verify_method_files(controls, protocol, data)
+        main_preds, main_rows = verify_method_files(main, protocol, data)
+        one_hot, _ = verify_method_files(OUT / 'one_hot_only' / name, protocol, data)
+        assert main_preds['one_hot'] == one_hot['one_hot']
+        replay, replay_rows = verify_method_files(OUT / 'cache_replay' / name, protocol, data)
+        assert main_preds == replay and main_rows == replay_rows
+        if name == 'development2000':
+            assert read(OUT / 'starter2000/protocol.json') == protocol
+            assert all(ranks == control_preds[method] for method, ranks in
+                       rankings(OUT / 'starter2000/predictions.csv').items())
+            case_map = read(main / 'case_customer_ids.json')
+            for case in read(main / 'cases.json').values():
+                uid = case_map[case['pseudonym']]
+                assert sorted(data.history[uid]) == [entry['ISIN'] for entry in case['history']]
+                assert sorted(data.truth[uid]) == case['truth']
+                for method, detail in case['methods'].items():
+                    saved_scores = read(main / detail['score_file'])
+                    assert detail['top10'] == main_preds[method][uid]
+                    assert detail['top10'] == [row['ISIN'] for row in saved_scores[:10]]
+                    assert detail['ndcg_at_10'] == main_rows[method, uid]['ndcg_at_10']
+                    assert [row['rank'] for row in saved_scores] == list(range(1, len(data.assets) + 1))
+                    assert saved_scores == sorted(saved_scores, key=lambda r: (-r['score'], -r['past_buyers'], r['ISIN']))
+            if (OUT / 'reference/run.json').exists():
+                reference, _ = verify_method_files(OUT / 'reference', protocol, data)
+                assert reference['original_text_cbf'] == control_preds['original_text_cbf']
+                summary['reference_control_ranks_equal'] = True
+        else:
+            assert read(hw2.HERE / 'outputs/official-reference/protocol.json') == protocol
+            assert rankings(hw2.HERE / 'outputs/official-reference/predictions.csv') == control_preds
+        summary[name] = {'users': length, 'protocol_hash': protocol['protocol_hash'],
+                         'verified_methods': sorted(control_preds.keys() | main_preds.keys())}
+    hw2.write_json(OUT / 'verification.json', summary)
+    print('Verified complete eligible rankings, recomputed per-user metrics and aggregates, matching '
+          'starter protocols, and pseudonymous case score evidence.')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
[EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md](<HOME>/Exocortex/Education/MiskaRis-2/llm4rec-far-trans/Vladislav/session3/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md) is ready for review.

All requested runs completed. The four classical baselines and one-hot reproduced the saved 100-user results at full precision. The file includes the 2,000-user results, short-history comparison, failure cases, and a pseudonymous hand-check case with full scores.

Both pinned models ran locally on Apple Silicon. The instructor reference used BF16 on MPS with batches of up to 24. Serial and batched outputs matched on all three smoke-test prompts. Predictions, per-user metrics, protocol hashes, and the native session log are saved locally.

Here is my interpretation, prepare the report, make it fast, use the same rules as before. Extract session and make it .json. Push to session3 when ready.

Interpretation:

On the 2,000-user development run, I found no improvement from replacing four-field one-hot encoding with frozen Qwen3 embeddings. With the metadata, purchase histories, candidate universe, and scorer held fixed, mean nDCG@10 fell from **0.0387 to 0.0366**. The first 100 users showed the opposite result, **0.0319 to 0.0403**, but they are part of the larger cohort and only 11 had eligible future purchases. I give more weight to the larger run and would test a separate time window before drawing a general conclusion.

For my main question about short purchase histories, the difference was smaller. Among the 55 users with one to three prior purchases and eligible future buys, Qwen improved 11 rankings by nDCG@10, worsened nine, and tied on 35. Despite winning more often than it lost, Qwen had a lower mean (**0.4769 vs. 0.4841**). The losses outweighed the gains in magnitude. With only 55 users contributing nonzero differences, I read this as limited evidence for retaining one-hot in this setup.

The individual cases helped me understand what the average hides. Qwen moved one relevant asset from rank 10 to 7, but in another case it pushed the user’s only future purchase from rank 9 to 15. I also saw a limitation shared by both encoders: assets with identical four-field metadata receive identical vectors. In one case, Qwen placed that tied group far enough down the ranking that the popularity tie-break left two relevant assets outside the top ten. A semantic encoder can change where a group ranks, but these four fields give it no way to distinguish assets within the group.

The instructor’s LLM-Rec encoder improved slightly over its own TF-IDF control (**0.0470 vs. 0.0464**) and required about **203 seconds** to generate the paraphrases. **Latest buy** led the full 2,000-user cohort at **0.0567**. For the next experiment, I would keep one-hot and recency as strong references and check whether either representation adds value for **new purchases versus repeat purchases** across prespecified cutoff dates.
I’m using the PDF skill to turn your interpretation and measured results into the report. I’ll also prepare the JSON session export and check the repository’s Session 3 destination before pushing.

Visual review alone is not a correctness check for a fillable PDF. A page `/Widget` annotation can render a value from its appearance stream while the canonical `/AcroForm/Fields` tree is missing or contains a stale value.

writer = PdfWriter()
writer.clone_document_from_reader(reader)

values_to_write = dict(expected_values)

    values_to_write = {
        name: field.get("/V", "/Off" if field.get("/FT") == "/Btn" else "")

    writer.remove_annotations(subtypes="/Widget")
    writer.root_object.pop(NameObject("/AcroForm"), None)

    writer.write(stream)

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: llm4rec-far-trans/Vladislav/session3/outputs/export_homework3_session.py
+from collections import Counter
+import csv
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import sys
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+NATIVE_LOG = Path(sys.argv[1])
+OUTPUT = ROOT / 'session3_neklyudov_vladislav_codex_session.json'
+CALLS = {'function_call', 'custom_tool_call'}
+RESULTS = {'function_call_output', 'custom_tool_call_output'}
+
+with (ROOT.parents[1] / 'data/FAR-Trans/customer_information.csv').open(encoding='utf-8-sig') as source:
+    customer_ids = {row['customerID'] for row in csv.DictReader(source)}
+
+jsonl = NATIVE_LOG.read_text().splitlines()
+native = []
+for i, line in enumerate(jsonl):
+    try:
+        native.append(json.loads(line))
+    except json.JSONDecodeError:
+        if i != len(jsonl) - 1:
+            raise
+
+trace = []
+for event in native:
+    if event['type'] != 'response_item':
+        continue
+    payload = event['payload']
+    kind = payload.get('type')
+    if kind == 'message' and payload.get('role') in {'user', 'assistant'}:
+        parts = payload.get('content', [])
+        if any(part.get('text', '').lstrip().startswith('<environment_context>') for part in parts):
+            continue
+    elif kind not in CALLS | RESULTS:
+        continue
+    clean = {k: v for k, v in payload.items() if not k.startswith('internal_')}
+    trace.append({'ordinal': event['ordinal'], 'timestamp': event['timestamp'], 'item': clean})
+
+result_ids = {row['item'].get('call_id') for row in trace if row['item']['type'] in RESULTS}
+trace = [row for row in trace if row['item']['type'] not in CALLS or row['item'].get('call_id') in result_ids]
+
+redactions = Counter()
+customer_pattern = re.compile(r'(?<![0-9A-F])[0-9A-F]{20}(?![0-9A-F])')
+secret_patterns = [
+    re.compile(r'\b(?:gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{25,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{30,}|hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{28,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{28,}|AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16})\b'),
+    re.compile(r'(?i)(?<=authorization: bearer )[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{18,}'),
+    re.compile(r'(?i)(?<=x-amz-signature=)[a-f0-9]{40,}'),
+]
+
+
+def scrub(value):
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return {k: scrub(v) for k, v in value.items()}
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return [scrub(v) for v in value]
+    if not isinstance(value, str):
+        return value
+
+    def customer(match):
+        if match.group() in customer_ids:
+            redactions['customer_id'] += 1
+            return '[customer ID redacted]'
+        return match.group()
+
+    text = customer_pattern.sub(customer, value)
+    for pattern in secret_patterns:
+        text, count = pattern.subn('[credential redacted]', text)
+        redactions['credential'] += count
+    redactions['home_path'] += text.count('<HOME>')
+    return text.replace('<HOME>', '<HOME>')
+
+
+trace = scrub(trace)
+counts = Counter(row['item']['type'] for row in trace)
+export = {
+    'schema_version': 1,
+    'format': 'Codex session transcript and tool trace, JSON derivative',
+    'title': 'Homework 3 — FAR-Trans paired encoders',
+    'export': {
+        'source': 'Native Codex JSONL for the experiment and report chat',
+        'records': 'Chronological user and assistant messages and completed tool calls and results. Each item retains the original native ordinal, timestamp, content or arguments, and call ID where present.',
+        'omissions': 'Internal instructions, reasoning, runtime telemetry, environment metadata, and tool calls awaiting a result when exported.',
+        'privacy': 'Local home prefixes are replaced. Tool content is checked for source customer IDs and credential patterns. Native JSONL is retained locally.',
+        'replacements': dict(redactions),
+    },
+    'counts': dict(counts),
+    'records': trace,
+}
+OUTPUT.write_text(json.dumps(export, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
+saved = json.loads(OUTPUT.read_text())
+assert saved == export
+assert sum(counts[k] for k in CALLS) == sum(counts[k] for k in RESULTS)
+assert any('Here is my interpretation' in json.dumps(row['item']) for row in trace if row['item'].get('role') == 'user')
+print(json.dumps({'counts': dict(counts), 'privacy_replacements': dict(redactions), 'bytes': OUTPUT.stat().st_size}))
*** End Patch"));
